description:
No spec subject (candidates: specled.append_only when picked up). Severity: Medium (calibrated down from spec auditor H1). From 2026-08-06 critical review of specled_-q0q. The self_authorized_weakening marker is emitted per (requirement, class) by the class-specific detectors; a requirement weakened via a path only one detector sees can surface differently depending on detector order. Keep-reason: unmade design decision — ticket q0q.2 simultaneously required uniform marker emission and forbade touching authorizing_decision/2, so a uniform-emission design (single choke point) needs its own decision + ADR. Concrete failure: a requirement weakened in class A while suppressed in class B can yield marker sets that depend on detector iteration order rather than a stated contract.

## ORCHESTRATOR CONTRACT (specled_-i4x)

Advances: specled.append_only

DECISION-CLASS: yes. Deliverable is an ADR + spec amendment + code. Per operator ruling on
epic specled_-i4x, draft it fully and record completion normally — the orchestrator will NOT
merge it without human sign-off.

WHERE THE TICKET IS MISLOCATED (read before designing): analyze/4
(lib/specled_ex/append_only.ex:100-115) runs detectors in a FIXED order and sort_findings/1
the result, so output is not "detector iteration order" dependent in the naive sense. The
ticket's claim is directionally right but points at the wrong mechanism. The three REAL
defects are:

1. authorizing_decision/2 (lib/specled_ex/append_only.ex:698-722) is Enum.reduce_while over
   `decisions`, halting on the FIRST ADR whose affects contains the id with a weakening
   change_type. self_authorized_marker_if_new/6 (:673-686) then tests only THAT ADR against
   new_adr_ids. With two ADRs authorizing the same requirement — one pre-existing, one
   new-in-diff — whether a marker is emitted depends purely on the order of `decisions`.
2. self_auth_adr_by_req_id/1 (:665-669) is a Map.put fold: with two new self-authorizing ADRs
   affecting the same requirement, the LAST one wins and is named in the marker message.
3. detect_requirement_deleted has a SECOND emission path (:132-138) that emits the marker
   straight from self_auth_adr_by_req_id without consulting authorizing_decision/2, while
   detect_must_downgraded (:172), detect_scenario_regression (:225) and
   detect_negative_removed (:264) all route through authorizing_decision/2 ->
   self_authorized_marker_if_new/6. Two authorization contracts, one function apart.

WHY A SPEC AMENDMENT IS UNAVOIDABLE: specled.append_only.self_authorized_weakening
(.spec/specs/append_only.spec.md:135-146) states NO cardinality and NO tie-break rule. The
"one marker per (requirement, weakening class)" contract exists only as a test comment
(test/specled_ex/append_only_test.exs:1255-1271). Your ADR must state the cardinality and the
tie-break, and the spec statement must carry it.

Allowed touches:
- lib/specled_ex/append_only.ex
- .spec/specs/append_only.spec.md
- .spec/decisions/specled.decision.*.md  (new ADR: uniform marker emission / authorization tie-break)
- test/specled_ex/append_only_test.exs
- test_support/append_only_fixtures.ex
- .spec/realization_hashes.json
- CHANGELOG.md

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/specled_ex/branch_check.ex
- lib/specled_ex/branch_check/severity.ex
- lib/specled_ex/review/html.ex
- lib/mix/tasks/**
- docs/**
- test/test_support/emitter_codes.ex

Out of Scope (intent):
- Do NOT add an ADR-status check to authorizing_decision/2. That is specled_-bg5.4, which is
  wired to depend on this ticket. Landing both blind produces two conflicting rewrites of the
  same function.
- Do NOT change :info severity or stdout rendering. That is specled_-bg5.5.
- Do NOT add a new append_only/* code — specled.decision.append_only_finding_budget_v2 governs
  the budget.
- Do NOT delete the self_auth_adr_by_req_id fast path without a stated replacement contract;
  it is what makes the superset-affects deletion scenario pass
  (.spec/specs/append_only.spec.md:344-354).

Verification:
  mix test test/specled_ex/append_only_test.exs
  mix test test/specled_ex/branch_check_test.exs
  mix compile --warnings-as-errors
  mix format --check-formatted
  mix spec.check --no-run-commands
  bash ./scripts/check_specs.sh
No execute:false stub to flip — .spec/specs/append_only.spec.md has zero execute:false entries.
New scenarios attach to the existing tagged_tests block (.spec/specs/append_only.spec.md:400-417),
already execute:true; add to its covers: only if a new requirement id is minted.

Expected diff: ~120-200 lines across 5-6 files (ADR ~60, append_only.ex ~40-60, spec ~10, tests ~60).

Session: 9a42db78-611e-4632-882a-adaefdaa666f

Mechanical checks:
- Files touched: 4 (.spec/decisions/specled.decision.uniform_self_authorization_markers.md, .spec/specs/append_only.spec.md, lib/specled_ex/append_only.ex, test/specled_ex/append_only_test.exs)

- realization_hashes.json unchanged and correct to be unchanged: baseline key is the MFA-scoped "SpecLedEx.AppendOnly.analyze/4" (.spec/realization_hashes.json:98), resolved_via beam, hasher_version 1. The diff changes analyze/4's body (one call-site arity change at :90) but adds no public export and does not alter analyze/4's head. `mix spec.check --no-run-commands` reports findings=0 with realization drift in scope -> no drift, so leaving the baseline untouched is correct.

The three named defects:
- (a) order-independent authorizer selection: CLOSED IN BEHAVIOR, UNDER-TESTED. authorizing_decision/3 (append_only.ex:672-700) now filters all matching decisions and picks via Enum.min_by on {not new?, adr_id}; false < true so new-in-diff wins. Test: "new authorizer wins over pre-existing authorizer regardless of decision order" (append_only_test.exs:854), asserts both [old, new] and [new, old] orders. Mutant caught (executed): replacing the selector with hd(authorizers) -> test fails with markers == [] under old-first order. Mutant NOT caught -> see Gap 1.
- (b) deterministic tie-break among new authorizers: CLOSED. Test: "lexicographically first new authorizer wins deletion tie regardless of order" (append_only_test.exs:905), both [d-a, d-z] and [d-z, d-a]. Mutant executed: hd(authorizers) -> fails, marker names `d-z` instead of `d-a`. assert_self_auth_marker/4 (:1348-1361) does `assert [marker] = markers`, so it also pins cardinality at exactly one per (requirement, class). self_auth_adr_by_req_id/1 is deleted (0 occurrences remain).
- (c) deletion-path second emission unified: CLOSED. detect_requirement_deleted (:115-142) now has the same shape as the other three: authorizing_decision/3 -> {:authorized, adr} -> self_authorized_marker_if_new/6. Verified all four call sites read identically (:118, :151, :204, :244) and no detector calls self_authorized_weakening_finding/5 directly any more. The fast path's replacement contract is stated in the ADR ("The deletion fast path is replaced by this shared selection rule. Superset `affects` deletion remains covered because every authorizing ADR is considered..."), and the superset scenario test at append_only_test.exs:658 passes on its own (`mix test ...:658` -> 1 test, 0 failures). self_authorizing_adrs/2 is retained and still feeds detect_same_pr_self_authorization/2 (:87, :102), so the per-ADR warning is untouched.

Spec amendment:
- Cardinality now stated in the must: "Exactly one marker shall be emitted per (requirement id, weakening class)."
- Tie-break now stated in the must: "When multiple ADRs authorize that pair, a new-in-diff ADR shall take precedence over a pre-existing ADR, then the lexicographically smallest ADR id shall break ties within the same newness class. The chosen ADR is independent of input decision order." Plus the corrected "authorized ONLY by ADRs already present at base shall emit no marker."
- ADR justifies both: yes. specled.decision.uniform_self_authorization_markers Decision section states the one-marker-per-pair rule and the 3-step selection (consider all weakening-set authorizers -> prefer new-in-diff -> lexicographic id), and Consequences calls the lexicographic key "a policy tie-break, not a chronology signal". ADR is registered in the subject's decisions: list (append_only.spec.md:39). It mints no finding code and does not collide with specled.decision.append_only_finding_budget_v2 (change_type: clarifies, no `replaces`, budget still 13 codes).

Append-only self-check:
- mix spec.check --no-run-commands findings against this diff: NONE. `branch base=origin/main changed_files=4 findings=0 (error=0 warning=0 info=0)`; re-run with --verbose (info shown) also reports 0. validate status=pass, spec.check result=pass. origin/main == bb64e69e, so the guard's base is the contract base.
- If a weakening finding fired, is it authorized by this diff's own ADR: no finding fired, and that is correct rather than lucky. The must statement is extended, not weakened: ModalClass sees "shall emit" on both sides (no downgrade), no requirement is deleted, scenario count goes UP by one (scenario.self_authorization_tie_break added), and no polarity is removed. The one clause edit — "authorized by" -> "authorized ONLY by" ADRs present at base — narrows the no-emit case, i.e. strengthens emission. Independently: the new ADR carries change_type: clarifies, which is NOT in @weakening_set, so it could not have authorized a weakening even if one existed; had this diff actually weakened the subject, append_only/requirement_deleted or must_downgraded would have fired as an error. So neither same_pr_self_authorization nor self_authorized_weakening is applicable to this diff.

Semantic checks:
- Out of Scope (intent) held: no ADR-status check in authorizing_decision/3 (the only "status" read in the module is the pre-existing adr_affects_widened check at :294, untouched by the diff) -> bg5.4 stays open; no severity or rendering change (marker still :info via self_authorized_weakening_finding/5, and lib/specled_ex/branch_check*, review/html.ex, mix/tasks/** are untouched); no new append_only/* code (diff adds zero `code:` literals); fast path deleted only with the ADR-stated replacement contract and the superset scenario still green.
- Spec stubs run: 0 executed (--no-run-commands tier; append_only.spec.md has zero execute:false entries, so none needed flipping).
- Targeted verification (all from the stage worktree, host `mix`): mix compile --warnings-as-errors -> clean; mix format --check-formatted -> clean; mix test append_only_test.exs + branch_check_test.exs -> 61 tests, 2 properties, 0 failures; mix spec.check --no-run-commands -> result=pass. Tree confirmed clean (git status --porcelain empty) after all mutation experiments were reverted.
- Full-suite verification: not run by verifier (by design)

Verdict: FAIL

Gaps (if FAIL):
- GAP 1 (single blocker, test-net only — production behavior is correct). The ADR's selection rule step 2, "prefer new-in-diff ADRs over ADRs already present at base", is NOT discriminated by any test. Executed proof: mutate authorizing_decision/3's min_by key from {not MapSet.member?(new_adr_ids, adr_id), adr_id || ""} to {adr_id || ""} — dropping the newness preference entirely, leaving a plain lexicographic sort — and the whole append_only suite stays GREEN (41 tests, 0 failures). The reason is fixture-id choice: the test at :854 names the pre-existing ADR "d-old" and the new one "d-new", and "d-new" < "d-old" lexicographically, so lexicographic order accidentally agrees with newness order. Renaming to pre-existing "d-aaa" / new "d-zzz" and re-running the same mutant makes it fail with markers == [] — i.e. the pre-existing ADR masks the same-diff self-authorization and NO marker is emitted, which is exactly defect F1 that this ticket exists to close. With the shipped code and the renamed ids the test passes, confirming production genuinely prefers the new ADR. Fix is two string literals in test/specled_ex/append_only_test.exs:854-897: pick ids where lexicographic order OPPOSES newness order (pre-existing lexicographically first, new-in-diff lexicographically last). Without it, a future simplification of the selector to a plain sort silently reintroduces F1 with CI green, and the spec/ADR rule has no enforcement.

Notes (advisory only, not blocking):
- The new scenario specled.append_only.scenario.self_authorization_tie_break carries `covers: []`, while its sibling scenario.self_authorized_weakening_marker covers specled.append_only.self_authorized_weakening. Validation passes either way, but the tie-break scenario is the one that now carries the amended must's cardinality + tie-break clauses; listing that requirement in its covers would make the spec-to-scenario link explicit.
- Minor behavior change not mentioned in the ADR: the :missing_change_type branch changed from last-match-wins (reduce_while overwriting acc) to first-match-wins (Enum.find). Immaterial — the returned decision is discarded at the only consumer (append_only.ex:134 binds it as _adr), and the actual append_only/missing_change_type findings come from the independent detect_missing_change_type/2 pass over all decisions. No test pins it. Worth one ADR sentence if bg5.4 touches this function again.
- self_authorized_marker_if_new/6 still re-checks new_adr_ids after the selector already ranked by newness. Harmless and correct (the selector may legitimately return a pre-existing ADR when no new one authorizes), just now a second-order guard rather than the primary decision.
